hints: Focus on the carbon atom bonded to the halogen, is it primary, secondary or tertiary in each case?
Remember that 1-iodopropane is primary, while both 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and 2-bromo-2-methylbutane are tertiary.
Link carbocation stability to mechanism, since only stable tertiary carbocations favour the two-step ionisation route of SN1.
walkthrough:
**Classify each halogenoalkane**

Great start, always look at the C-X carbon first. Count how many other carbons are attached to it.

$\text{1-iodopropane: CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{I}$ is primary, $\text{2-iodo-2-methylpropane: (CH}_3)_3\text{CI}$ is tertiary, $\text{2-bromo-2-methylbutane: CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(Br)(CH}_3)_2$ is tertiary.

**Recall what SN1 needs**

SN1 goes in two steps with a carbocation intermediate. Think of it as break first, then make.

$$\text{R}_3\text{C-X} \rightarrow \text{R}_3\text{C}^+ + \text{X}^- \text{ (slow ionisation)}$$ 
$$\text{R}_3\text{C}^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R}_3\text{C-OH} \text{ (fast attack)}$$

**Match stability to mechanism**

Tertiary carbocations are stabilised by electron donation from three alkyl groups, so they form easily. Primary carbocations are too unstable, so primary halogenoalkanes avoid SN1 and go by SN2 instead.

That means 1 reacts mainly by SN2, while 2 and 3 react mainly by SN1.

options.A: Incorrect. Statement 1 is 1-iodopropane, a primary halogenoalkane. It forms a very unstable primary carbocation, so it reacts mainly by SN2, not SN1.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination includes the primary halogenoalkane 1. Students sometimes choose this by focusing only on the good leaving group iodide and forgetting that carbon type controls the mechanism.
options.C: Correct. Both 2 and 3 are tertiary halogenoalkanes. They form stable tertiary carbocations on ionisation, so both hydrolyse with NaOH(aq) mainly by the SN1 mechanism.
options.D: Incorrect. Not all three are SN1. While 2 and 3 are tertiary and SN1, 1 is primary and reacts mainly by SN2. This trap comes from thinking all hydrolysis with NaOH(aq) is SN1.
